html:
The Kurrama, also known as the Puutu Kunti Kurrama, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Pilbara in Western Australia, in the country of the Hamersley Range and the Robe and Ashburton rivers. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.

Their neighbours included the Pinikura to the south, the Nhuwala to the west, the Martuthunira to the north and the Jiwarli to the southeast. The Puutu Kunti Kurrama and the Pinikura, though of different language groups, now manage their lands through one corporation.

Their country is rich in iron ore and has been mined on a huge scale since the 1960s. In 2020 Rio Tinto destroyed the ancient rock shelters at Juukan Gorge on their land to expand a mine, a loss that shocked Australia and led to a national inquiry into how heritage is protected.
